status: design frozen before AES baseline implementation/metrics
purpose: Test whether conventional encryption with an ordinary private transaction provides the same useful functionality
cipher: AES-128 in CTR mode, following NIST SP800-38A
counter_uniqueness: Tags are unique1..N and D/128 is public. All counters are distinct under one epoch AES key and fit128bits. Every accepted epoch uses an independent fresh key. No probabilistic nonce overlap assumption is needed.
metadata: Stable unique tie tags already exist as secret shared state in R1 for deterministic ranking; they are not opened or stored with public ciphertexts
key_bundle: One locator-permutation key plus one AES key, independently sampled. Canonical128-bit encoding of uniform Fp AES key has statistical distance (2^128-p)/2^128 from uniform128-bit keys; report this explicitly.
plaintext_packing: Pack root coordinate bits MSB-first into bytes; XOR AES-CTR keystream. Masks and decryption are computed only on secret wires in MPC.
transition: Decode old ciphertext transiently in MPC, encrypt under new epoch key, update private index using full-width compact sort/merge; verify same old/new-root and proposed-index invariant, then same selection/shuffle/share-refresh/persistence
additional_control: AES with the direct locator update isolates mask-generation costs from index-translation costs. Before all secure AES metrics, add the same stable-secret-handle representation to AES and MiMC atN8/32: encryption comparisons must not conflate cipher cost with physical-index rewriting. The same two-field global key bundle is retained; the virtual locator key defines the semantic interpretation without per-slot evaluation.
same_candidate_query: Compute ordinary decryption/Hamming inside MPC, or equivalent probe masking; assert exact scores against an independent AES oracle
authentication_scope: CTR supplies confidentiality. The same separate application consistency checker supplies the compared transition-integrity contract under passive MPC. This is not an AES-GCM or malicious-MPC claim.
implementation_plan: Use a primary Bristol Fashion AES circuit with arithmetic-shared bit gates, preserving the five-party degree-two Shamir backend. Verify NIST known-answer vectors and bit order first; precompute key-only wire expressions once per mask call where possible.
independent_oracle: A separate standard AES library; do not reuse the circuit evaluator as the only reference
interpretation: This is a representative standard-encryption implementation under the chosen arithmetic MPC backend, not a lower bound on all AES implementations. Equivalent functionality or better cost is retained and may narrow the M-SLE novelty claim.
